quest.title: Confessions of an Outlander
quest.description: You arrive at Ritou in Inazuma smoothly and meet up with your contact, Thoma. But it seems that outlanders are far from welcome here...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x800, Primogem x30, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

chapter.title: The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia

talks.objective: Go register at the border checkpoint with Thoma

dialogues.speaker: Kageyama
dialogues.text: Hello, please state your name, identity, and the purpose of your visit. Oh, except you, Thoma.

dialogues.speaker: Kageyama
dialogues.text: You must be... new here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Heh...

dialogues.speaker: Kageyama
dialogues.text: Excuse me? Please provide the information requested, and also declare any goods you are carrying with you.

choices.text: We are here to... trade wine. And ore.

response.speaker: Kageyama
response.text: Currently, only members of the International Trade Association are authorized to engage in the import and export of goods. Do you have your trader's permits?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... uh... w—we—uh...

response.speaker: Kageyama
response.text: My apologies, but I'll have to ask you to—

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Here are their entry papers, for your kind perusal.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!? Ugh, take your time! No rush or anything!

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Haha, I just wanted to see what you'd say... sorry about that.

response.speaker: Kageyama
response.text: ...I see, okay. Your papers are all in order. Welcome to Ritou.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Pheeeew...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, where do we go next?

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: The Outlander Affairs Agency.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: They only check entry permits here. If you want to remain on Ritou, there's a process you have to go through with them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sheesh, so it is super strict, just like everyone says.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Well, let's not forget that to everyday folk in Inazuma, people from everywhere else are referred to as "outsiders."

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: As the word suggests, outlanders aren't very welcome in Inazuma with the Sakoku Decree in force.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Not even on Ritou, where they've established an Outsider Settlement.

choices.text: Welcome or not, we don't have a choice.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Hehe, I like how you think. I've got a feeling we're going to get along very well.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Now. Let's head over to the Outlander Affairs Agency.

choices.text: My journey must go on.
#We are here to find my {F#brother}{M#sister}.

response.speaker: Kageyama
response.text: Oh? Well, I'm sorry. We cannot approve entry for purely personal reasons. So, unless you have a valid reason for visiting in accordance with the rules...

talks.objective: Go process your application at the Outlander Affairs Agency with Thoma

dialogues.speaker: Yurika
dialogues.text: You've completed the entry procedures, yes? And now you want to apply for residency? Both of you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yes, please!

dialogues.speaker: Yurika
dialogues.text: Okay. The processing fee will be two million Mora.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: T—Two million! For a processing fee? Are you serious!?

dialogues.speaker: Yurika
dialogues.text: That's right, one million per applicant, which makes two million total. Don't worry, you can trust my math.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon wasn't so much questioning your math as... Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Hahaha... Ma'am, these two here are good friends of mine. I think you'll find I'm one face you recognize.

dialogues.speaker: Yurika
dialogues.text: Ah, Mr. Thoma, it's you. By way of courtesy, allow me to reduce it to 400,000 Mora total.

choices.text: That's still quite expensive...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Thank you ever so much, Miss Yurika.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: But as this is just a processing fee... I think 600 Mora should cover it if I'm paying on their behalf? I'll treat you to dinner, too. How does that sound?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's not how you haggle! By all means, bargain the price down, but—

response.speaker: Yurika
response.text: Alright then. As you wish, Mr. Thoma. I will make a record.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Hee-hee, much obliged.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!? She went from two million down to 600? There's something seriously wrong with people's sense of finance around here!

choices.text: I think it's about more than the Mora.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Hehe, it's not as mind-boggling as you think. "Processing fee" is just a figure of speech.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: The way some here at the agency see it, the fees are easy money, so it becomes a question of how much they can make.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: So when the day comes that some poor merchant from overseas with more money than sense gets stuck here and needs to apply for residency...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then they'll milk them for all they're worth!

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Exactly. It's at times like this that having a local friend really comes in handy.

choices.text: That's blatant oppression against outlanders...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Yes, but when you're an outlander in Inazuma, far from home, in this closed-nation era, there's very little that can be done about it.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: The most that overseas merchants can do to look after themselves is stick together.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: That's how the International Trade Association came about.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So it's a trade association built by and for outlanders?

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Yep, and as well as advancing commercial interests, the association provides help, support, and structure for outlanders trying to survive on Ritou.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Essentially, it's an association devoted to both commercial excellence and survival skills.

choices.text: So how would an outlander ever get to meet...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Sounds like just stayin' alive is an achievement when you're an outlander in Inazuma...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: I see... so this is the real purpose of your trip. Yes, given that you are outlanders, it's certainly a lofty aspiration.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: After all, the Raiden Shogun is the most exalted and revered one in all of Inazuma. She is a deity who reigns on high, while all other life gazes up in awe.

choices.text: That may well be...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: I was going to say, nothing is set in stone when it comes to who you will encounter in this world. Who's to say you won't happen to run into the Raiden Shogun one day after lunch...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-huh... And is that likely...?

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Okay, I'll give it to you straight. I know of a way to introduce you to the Raiden Shogun.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really!? Wow, the Ritou fixer is better connected than we thought!

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Ahem, hehe — I mean, it will take all the resources I have at my disposal, but it can be done. However, before we get there...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Connections come at a high price, you understand?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, not you too!

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Hahaha! No, no... In this instance, when I say price, I'm not talking about Mora.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: In fact, there's no real cost, as such. It's just that... if this is something you really want, you'll have to agree to help other people solve some of their problems first.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: I like to do things in a way that keeps everybody happy. It's my own personal rule for dealing with situations like this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds very reasonable to Paimon! You're the man in the middle, so you have to trade favors to keep everyone indebted to you.

choices.text: The fixer works in mysterious ways...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Heh... Why do I get the feeling you're making me out to be some sort of crook... Uh, never mind.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Here's the situation. As I touched upon earlier, the members of the International Trade Association are constantly struggling to survive.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Recently, things seem to have gotten more difficult than ever for them. So just go and check things out, see if there's any way you can help.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: The head of the association is called Kurisu, and he's a good friend of mine. Go talk to him, I'll wait for you here.

choices.text: So, what's the job?
I still have to find a way!
The Raiden Shogun feels further away than ever...
Doesn't anyone push back?
Reminds me of someone else's strange relationship with Mora...
That is a major discount...

talks.objective: Go to the International Trade Association and understand its members' situation

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Oh? Hello there, you must be seeking refuge with the International Trade Association. The Outlander Affairs Agency took you for all you're worth, I suppose.

choices.text: Very nearly...

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: Ah, good, that's a relief. *sigh* ...You need to be careful, or you'll find yourself losing your savings all at once.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We heard the association has been having some difficulties lately. Is that true?

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: Yes... left, right, and center. Obstacles at every turn. But that's nothing new for us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Sakoku Decree certainly makes things difficult for anyone who wants to come here from overseas.

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: But it's not the root cause of our woes. The Sakoku Decree might restrict our scope of activity, but in and of itself it doesn't stop us from being able to enjoy a comfortable existence.

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: No, what's really squeezing us outlander merchants dry is...

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: ...those Mora-grubbers from the Kanjou Commission.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, of the three Commissions, that's the one that oversees everything on Ritou, isn't it?

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: That's right. They impose astronomical tax rates, unbelievable regulations, and that's not the worst of it...

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: They just issued a new Tax Decree recently that, for some reason, completely changes the way we pay our taxes. It used to be Mora, but now it's something called Crystal Marrow.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Crystal Marrow...? What's that?

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: Something that most of us in the association had never heard of before either, until the new decree came along.

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: Eventually, one of the older Liyue merchants recalled that he once shipped a batch of it to Snezhnaya in his youth.

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: So in order to pay our taxes, we began an arduous search for this Crystal Marrow.

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: But then we found we'd only managed to create a bigger problem for ourselves. The rising demand for Crystal Marrow drove the price higher and higher...

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: Now, there's only one vendor who even has it in stock. We can't get hold of it anywhere else...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... isn't that what they call a monopoly?

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: Exactly. So this vendor keeps pushing the price up, and we have no choice but to buy from them because the Tax Decree forces us to...

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: It's a vicious cycle, the consequence of which is that our taxes will soon exceed our profits... and once that happens...

choices.text: This is absurd treatment.

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: We've tried communicating with the commission directly...

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: But this is a nation where the cries of a few struggling merchants will never be heard over the ever-present roar of thunder...

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: *sigh* Fontaine, my dear homeland... I miss you an awful lot at the moment...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds awful, they're really bleeding them dry.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, what do you think we should do?

choices.text: Try our best to negotiate with the Kanjou Commission?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Kurisu's the head of the association and even he hasn't had any luck. Not to mention, we're outlanders too...

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: Right, and besides... I think this may well be the fate they've ordained for us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, well we could try tackling the problem by going to the other party involved...

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: *sigh* That vendor...

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: I've actually done business with him in the past, but after a point, he stopped contacting us. I have no idea where he sources the stuff...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Well, it definitely sounds like he's being unfair. How do we find him? We could go talk to him and see if he lets anything slip.

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: Hey, that's a pretty good idea! Since you're not affiliated with the association and you're new to Ritou, he may just let his guard down.

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: If I remember correctly, our usual meeting point with him is under a tree by the coast in the residential district. See if you can find him there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Got it! We're on the case!

choices.text: The vendor does sounds like a fishy character.
Can't you discuss the situation with the Kanjou Commission?
Luckily, we had a friend with us.

talks.objective: Find the merchant selling Crystal Marrow

dialogues.speaker: Werner
dialogues.text: Hm? I don't think I recognize you, are you new arrivals?

choices.text: Yes, we just arrived.

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: Haha, very funny. Real "Fixers" don't need to refer to themselves that way. I wasn't born yesterday, you know.

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: So. What do you need with me?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Where do you source your goods?

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: The sheer nerve! You don't go around asking questions like that! If I gave you my sources, I might as well hand you the whole darn business!

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: Trade secret, got it? You know what "trade" and "secret" mean, right? Tsk.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This guy's got a bad attitude...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Can you... reduce your prices?

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: Hah! Are you even buying!? ...Ohh, I see what's going on here. Kurisu and his associates sent you here to try and plead their case, didn't they?

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: Heh, they're wasting their time. The price is non-negotiable, not by a single Mora.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, what's your problem!?

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: Get out of here, go on. Tell them they're lucky to be buying from me in the first place, and they ought to be more grateful. If it weren't for me, they'd be in seriously hot water.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What are we gonna do? There's no talking to this guy...

choices.text: Time to get the real fixer on the case...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good idea. Let's check back in with him.

choices.text: Let's go talk to Thoma.
You don't recognize me? But I'm the fixer 'round these parts!

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Hm? That was quick... You resolved it already?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, actually we're having a little trouble...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're going to have to help us help you.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Oh? Well, by all means, tell me what you need. I'll help as much as I can.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Getting you to go fixing things when you've only just arrived is quite a demand.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you know about Werner?

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Oh, that guy? I'm familiar.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: He used to be a bit of a sorry sight, selling shells that he'd collect on the beach just to get by. But he seems to have suddenly shot up in the world recently.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: I can only assume he must have found himself a patron after leaving the International Trade Association.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You're saying he used to be a member of the International Trade Association? So he's an outlander, too?

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Yes... couldn't you tell when you spoke to him?

choices.text: Seemed like a Mondstadter to me.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: That's right, Werner was born in Mondstadt, then went into the shipping business, trading between Liyue and Inazuma.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: When Inazuma closed to the outside world, he was one of a group of outlanders that ended up stranded on Ritou.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, what a bummer...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: The International Trade Association was initially very generous to him, but over time, with decree after decree, the association members found it increasingly difficult to make ends meet...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, he left the association and turned his back on them!

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Haha, I'm sure it's more nuanced than that. I believe even the most ungrateful and cold-hearted of people still have some amount of gratitude and warmth left in them somewhere.

choices.text: Got it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? Is that all you need to know?

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Well then, it sounds like you may have found a way in with him.

choices.text: I'll go back and talk to him again.
At least, I didn't get the impression he was a local.

dialogues.speaker: Werner
dialogues.text: What are you doing back here? Just 'cause I got plenty of time on my hands doesn't mean I want to waste any of it talking to you.

choices.text: Time on your hands... Some would call that a form of freedom.

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: Huh? Where's this coming from...

choices.text: A Dandelion Wine would sure be nice on a day like this...
A bard's serenade would be perfect right now...
It was the wind that led me back here to you.

talks.objective: Show Werner the goods from Mondstadt

dialogues.speaker: Werner
dialogues.text: ...Mondstadt... You're talking about... Mondstadt?

dialogues.speaker: Werner
dialogues.text: Goodness, I can sense it now. So familiar, but I can't remember the last time I was there...

dialogues.speaker: Werner
dialogues.text: Ah, the scent of Mondstadt... Oh, how it takes me back...

choices.text: May the Anemo Archon protect you.

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: *sigh* My hometown... The home of freedom...! How I long to go back and visit...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, it's working...

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: Ah... Oh — ahem! So, trying to play my heartstrings like a lyre are you? I know what you're up to.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Close your eyes...

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: Huh? What is this, what are you up to now?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Just close your eyes already!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Listen closely... doesn't it sound familiar...?

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: You mean... the sound of the ocean?

choices.text: Cheap 'n' tasty chop suey!

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: *gasp* Liyue Harbor! I can see it so clearly! Oh, and the sound of the waves, the calls of the merchants...

choices.text: May the flames of virtue spread to all...

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: Xiao Lanterns! Haha, I'm right there, at the Lantern Rite! Oh... look at them, floating up into the sky!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This guy has a really active imagination... either that or he really does miss Liyue Harbor...

choices.text: ...and never be extinguished!
Grilled Tiger Fish, get it while it's hot!
Let the Wind lead.

talks.objective: Show Werner the goods from Liyue

dialogues.speaker: Werner
dialogues.text: *sigh* Liyue, Liyue...

dialogues.speaker: Werner
dialogues.text: Wait... Stop, that's enough... Don't make me relive it any more, my poor heart can't take it...

choices.text: A lot of people out there sympathize with the position you're in.

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: You mean... the folks from the International Trade Association... And I suppose they are far from home, just like me.

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: Often, I'll sneak down to the shore at night and listen to the sound of the waves... I like to imagine it's the voice of my hometown, carried across the ocean.

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: I've run into folks from the association more than a few times doing just that, but I always hide my face and slip away...

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: *sigh* Don't you think I've wanted to talk things through with them, and free myself from this anguish?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... well, no one's stopping you, so...

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: They're so resilient. None of them had anyone else to rely on, so they rallied together, committed to finding a way to survive... But I couldn't do it, I'm not strong enough...

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: So... I caved... Those people, they'd make the smallest of promises, offer the most measly benefits, and I'd do whatever they asked of me... and make Mondstadters look like the worst people in the world...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Who are "those people"?

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: ...Alright, I'll tell you the whole story. It's eating me up inside and I can't take it anymore.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're ready to talk now?

choices.text: The International Trade Association will protect you.

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: But I betrayed them... I can't show my face there...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, c'mon you scaredy-cat! Look, you messed up, but now it's time to make things right!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, come on, get it off your chest. What's the deal here?

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: It's a scheme by the tax-collection ashigaru. Keijirou and his companions.

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: They start by overtaxing the merchants, then take the extra Crystal Marrow they receive and stockpile it.

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: Once the merchants run out of places to buy Crystal Marrow, they get me to sell that extra stock back to the merchants at an extortionate price, with the proceeds going to the tax-collection ashigaru.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's just... it's plain evil, gouging them like this.

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: I'm their puppet, yes... but my cut is a tiny fraction of what we take in total. It's barely enough for me to live on.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We need evidence.

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: Evidence? Hmm... You're right, without conclusive evidence, he will never admit it.

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: Now that I think about it, whenever I report back to him after a sale, he always heads to the same place. It's always made me suspicious...

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: As it happens, I handed some Mora over to him not long ago. I can show you where he went if you want.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? Well, then there's no time to lose! Let's go.

choices.text: Come get a drink with your friends from the association.
A lot of people have supported you in the past.

dialogues.speaker: Werner
dialogues.text: Keijirou! It's him!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: After him!

dialogues.speaker: Werner
dialogues.text: What could he be doing at a place like this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It looked like he buried something over there, didn't it? Why don't we take a look?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, it's... a ledger...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Boring... Paimon thought he'd hidden a big pile of Mora here.

choices.text: Ah yes, the real reason Paimon came along.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ehehe, yeah...

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: Let me take a look here...

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: Aha, yes. This is what we're looking for. A clear and complete record of every single transaction, each one proof of his guilt.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Great! Well, now we have our hard evidence, let's go tell Kurisu the good news, shall we?

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: Ah, um... I—I'll say goodbye to you here, then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? You aren't gonna come with us?

response.speaker: Werner
response.text: I... I need a little more time before I'm ready to face the head of the association. I'm sorry.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Poor Werner's a pretty awkward guy, huh...

choices.text: Even if we did find Mora, we would give it to the trade association.

talks.objective: Tell the International Trade Association about what really happened

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: But we really don't have anything left. If this keeps up, our sales will come in at a loss. There'll be nothing left for us to do but starve...

dialogues.speaker: Keijirou
dialogues.text: You know the decree. The rules are the rules. No discounts, no exceptions — and no excuses!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're the one making a mockery of the rules here, Keijirou!

dialogues.speaker: Keijirou
dialogues.text: Hmm? And who are you? Another new member of the association?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It just so happens that we found your little ledger. So now we're here to tell everyone all about how you embezzled Crystal Marrow to sell it right back to the tax payers!

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Huh? Is this true!?

dialogues.speaker: Harrison
dialogues.text: You've been swindling us!

dialogues.speaker: Keijirou
dialogues.text: Well, uh... You see... The t—taxes, uh...

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Let me take a look at the ledger.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Text on a black screen: Kurisu reads aloud every entered transaction in full.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Well would you look at that... Every payment the association has made is right here in your personal ledger.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: So, Mr. Keijirou, it seems you have some explaining to do. How shall we settle this, hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Keijirou
dialogues.text: Hmph! So you think you can use this against me do you? I—It's quite obvious that I'm merely trying to earn a modest living for myself, like anyone else...!

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Word has it that samurai in the commission place great importance on reputation and prestige... Though, I'm sure commission members won't blame you once word gets out...

dialogues.speaker: Keijirou
dialogues.text: Huh? Is that a threat? Are you threatening me!?

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: No, not at all. I'm simply stating that it would be quite a pity if an illustrious gentleman such as yourself were to have their reputation tarnished.

dialogues.speaker: Keijirou
dialogues.text: Uhh... W—Well even if what you say is true, what do you suggest we do about it...?

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: I believe you still have a quantity of Crystal Marrow in your possession, correct?

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Perhaps that Crystal Marrow could be used as compensation for the recent tax hike, and us merchants could finally have some more breathing room.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that it?

dialogues.speaker: Keijirou
dialogues.text: Hmph, do you have any idea the hoops I had to jump through to get the Crystal Marrow and keep it hidden!? Ugh, fine! In that case, I'll send it over to you today.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And not even an ounce of shame for his actions...

dialogues.speaker: Harrison
dialogues.text: So that's it!? My shop's been closed for weeks now — I've even had to ask my friends to help bail me out! What about my losses!?

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Come on, Harrison! We've already struck a good deal here...

dialogues.speaker: Harrison
dialogues.text: I'm sick of being pushed around like this! I won't let him off so easily!

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Harrison!

dialogues.speaker: Katsuie
dialogues.text: Hey! What's all this racket? Does someone dare question the decree?

dialogues.speaker: Keijirou
dialogues.text: Ah, Chief. You've arrived.

dialogues.speaker: Katsuie
dialogues.text: What was all the commotion I heard just now?

dialogues.speaker: Keijirou
dialogues.text: Oh, we were just discussing a minor tax issue. I do my utmost to lend them a helping hand, but they're never grateful.

dialogues.speaker: Harrison
dialogues.text: A helping hand!? The only thing you're doing is stuffing your greedy pockets with our hard-earned wealth. I assure you that Hiiragi Shinsuke will hear of this!

dialogues.speaker: Katsuie
dialogues.text: Oh? And you dare to utter the Commissioner's name? You outlanders have no respect for the rules.

dialogues.speaker: Katsuie
dialogues.text: Seize the merchants! We will resolve this dispute back at headquarters!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh-oh, this is going in a bad direction...

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Gentlemen, gentlemen. Come now, is there any need for this? If there's a dispute to resolve, let's get a drink and talk it over.

dialogues.speaker: Keijirou
dialogues.text: Who are you supposed to be? And why in my right mind would I join you for a drink?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ha! You never heard of the fixer!?

choices.text: Context, Paimon, context...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Here's my card...

response.speaker: Katsuie
response.text: Huh... you're from the Yashiro Commission?

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Shh...

response.speaker: Katsuie
response.text: Hmph, well, this is Kanjou Commission territory. However powerful the Yashiro Commission may be, you have no business meddling in Ritou's affairs.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Of course not. Of course not. Still, perhaps you could show the young lady of our clan some courtesy...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: You wouldn't want your names showing up in a petition to the shogun, would you?

response.speaker: Katsuie
response.text: That fan... the Shirasagi Himegimi.

response.speaker: Katsuie
response.text: ...I don't need any trouble with her. Okay, let's forget all this. It'll give us one less thing to worry about.

response.speaker: Keijirou
response.text: But Chief...

response.speaker: Katsuie
response.text: Enough! We're leaving.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Let's get dinner one day soon, gentlemen. My treat. I insist.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Eh, no response, huh... I suppose that bridge is well and truly burned, then.

response.speaker: Kurisu
response.text: Thank you so much, Thoma... But I'm sorry your relationship with the Kanjou Commission had to suffer for our sake...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: #Haha. Hey, hey, I was joking. It's a small price to pay and you're more than welcome. If there's anyone you should be thanking, it's the Traveler. {F#She's}{M#He's} the one who found a way to turn things around.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: If nothing else, I'm sure the tax-collection ashigaru will tread a little more carefully in future.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thoma... what was all that—

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Shh... Not here, too many people listening, haha. Let's move somewhere else.

choices.text: That title doesn't have any weight with these people.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Corruption seems rife in the Kanjou Commission, they truly are rotten to the core... *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Alright. Time for me to answer your questions. What would you like to know?

choices.text: Tell me about the Yashiro Commission.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Haha, straight to the point. Let me re-introduce myself.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: I belong to the Kamisato Clan of the Yashiro Commission on Narukami Island. I'm an attendant of the Shirasagi Himegimi.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, you've been keeping your true identity a secret from us this whole time!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, the Yashiro Commission. Guessing that's another branch of the Tri-Commission?

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Correct. The Kamisato Clan is the head of the Yashiro Commission, who manage ceremonial and cultural affairs. I'd go into more detail on what exactly that covers, but I'm not even sure myself.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: I'm just someone who was fortunate enough to be taken in by the Kamisato Clan. My role is to take care of the daughter of the clan — Kamisato Ayaka, also known as the Shirasagi Himegimi.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seems like she must be super-famous in Inazuma, given the reaction of those guys just now.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Hahaha... Oh, most definitely. She's graceful, dignified, and kind-hearted, too. The people of Inazuma quite adore Miss Kamisato.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Her fame even somewhat eclipses that of her older brother, Kamisato Ayato, despite the fact that he is the current head of the clan.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: I suppose those who treat others with compassion earn themselves the same treatment in return. Miss Kamisato's situation certainly seems to attest to that. Take me, for example — I'm just an attendant, and yet she treats me as an equal, as she would a friend.

choices.text: So where did this "fixer of Ritou" thing come from?

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: You're asking the right questions. And to be honest, I don't want to keep you in the dark any more than is necessary.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Firstly, you should know that being a fixer is not something you can fake. I spent the better part of a month tirelessly building up a network of relationships on the island, and I got to know Captain Beidou during that time, too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still pretty good going for just a month's work!

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Haha, well, maybe I have a slight knack for schmoozery. But the main thing was, I had to make sure I'd be in time to receive you when you arrived.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Inazuma may have closed off to the outside world, but that hasn't stopped a lot of people from hearing about your feats in Mondstadt and Liyue.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: So, when Miss Kamisato heard of your intention to come to Inazuma, she began looking forward to your arrival with great anticipation. She's excited to find out whether the rumors are true...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: ...that is, that you have what it takes to change the tide of the times.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Change the tide of the times?

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: In the test that I gave you earlier, although there were a few hiccups at the end, it was you who found the way to turn the situation around.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Navigating powerful people, using their character flaws to your advantage... it's just what Miss Kamisato had hoped to see.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: With your help... even the Vision Hunt Decree—

choices.text: I never offered to help.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Hmm, that's an unexpected development. Perhaps our sources were misleading...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I have one goal here: to meet the Raiden Shogun.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: ...Yes, of course. I completely understand, and as agreed, I shall help set that up for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, Thoma sure didn't put up much of a fight...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Hah... Well, my work on Ritou is done, so I suppose this is goodbye for now.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Oh, one more thing — this Invitation Letter is for you... When you get to Narukami Island, you can find me at Komore Teahouse, as per the letter.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Good luck with everything. See you soon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thoma's not such a bad guy, huh. We should get going.

choices.text: But...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What's up?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Outlanders are unable to leave Ritou.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right! Paimon forgot all about that!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, so... did Thoma forget that, too?

choices.text: I think perhaps not...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Darn it! Grr, no wonder he was so matter-of-fact about the whole thing!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: As soon as we get off Ritou, Paimon's going straight to Komore Teahouse to settle the score!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, well, guess we should give it a try. Let's head to the border and see how far we get.

choices.text: This must be the next part of his "test."
There is one problem...
I refuse.
So as her attendant... are we helping you or her...?
Tell me about the Shirasagi Himegimi.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Kurisu will reach his wits' end if things carry on like they are. Go see what you can do for him.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: I can't thank you enough for helping me out. If you've got no place to go, you're always welcome at the International Trade Association.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Something tells me you've come up with a smart way to solve this...

dialogues.speaker: Werner
dialogues.text: Hmph. I'm the only lifeline they've got. How dare they try and bargain with me!

dialogues.speaker: Harrison
dialogues.text: It's tyranny — plain and simple...

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Thank you so much, our heads are back above water now...

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Most of the current rules were put in place by the administration of Ritou — the Kanjou Commission.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Kanjou Commission?

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Yes, one branch of the Tri-Commission of Inazuma. Responsible for growing and managing the nation's wealth. Um... you really haven't heard of it before?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems we got back just in time — Keijirou looks like he's about to collect more taxes. Quick, let's head over!

dialogues.speaker: Keijirou
dialogues.text: Now, who else is behind on payments?

dialogues.speaker: Keijirou
dialogues.text: Let me think... yes, the trade association clique still need to be brought into line.

dialogues.speaker: Keijirou
dialogues.text: Hm? What was that sound...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Shh... Quiet! Don't let him find us!

dialogues.speaker: Keijirou
dialogues.text: Must be hearing things. Drat, I'm behind schedule. I need to hurry...

dialogues.speaker: Keijirou
dialogues.text: Come out. I can see you.

dialogues.speaker: Keijirou
dialogues.text: Who are you, and why are you following me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh-oh, seems like he's noticed us...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Where'd he go?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He was right there a moment ago... Seems he disappeared in the blink of an eye.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If only we'd made less noise..

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's getting further and further away. Let's catch up a little.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Too close, that's too close! He'll notice us for sure!
